title: First steps with Byte
reflection: Why is it useful to save instructions in a program instead of typing them one at a time?

steps.goal: In Byte's terminal, first type edit hello to start the program; in it, make your Byte say something in chat with mine.say, then save and run it.
steps.block_goal: Make your Byte say something in chat with the "say" block, then run the program.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: your program has to make Byte speak with mine.say.
hints: Check that the terminal's line starts with > and not with lua> (type exit() to leave lua), then type edit hello.
In the editor write mine.say("Hi!"). Press Ctrl, pick Save with the arrows and press Enter; then Ctrl again, Exit, Enter. In the terminal type hello and press Enter.
block_hints: In Byte group, drag the "say" block into the white area and write something in it.
Press Run ▶ and go back to Minecraft: after 3, 2, 1 your Byte speaks in the chat.

steps.goal: Write a new program (edit roundtrip) that takes Byte 3 blocks forward and back to where it started, facing the same way.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: Byte has to go at least 3 blocks away and come back to where it started, facing the same way.
hints: Plan it on paper first: how many steps forward? How many turns to face back?
To turn around, turn twice: byte.turnLeft() two times. At the end, turn twice again.
block_hints: Plan it on paper first: how many steps forward? How many turns to face back?
To turn around, use "turn left" twice. At the end, turn twice again.

steps.goal: Write a new program (edit tower) that builds a tower 3 blocks tall in front of Byte, then brings Byte back down.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: build a tower 3 blocks tall right in front of where Byte started, and bring Byte back down.
hints: Byte needs blocks: put at least 3 in the highlighted slot of its 4x4 inventory, all in that same slot.
Place a block, go up, place a block... then come back down.
block_hints: Byte needs blocks: put at least 3 in the highlighted slot of its 4x4 inventory, all in that same slot.
"place a block in front", "move up", "place a block in front"... then "move down" until Byte is back on the ground.
